passage.title: Stress less
paragraphs: How busy is too busy? For some, it means sometimes having to have a short lunch; for others, it may mean missing lunch altogether. For a few, it is not being able to take a day off once a month. Then there is a group of people for whom working every evening and weekend is normal, and feeling stressed is taken for granted. For most senior executives, workloads swing between extremely busy and frenzied. Neil Plumridge, vice-president of a management consultancy company, says that his weeks vary from a ’manageable 45 hours to 80 hours, but average 60 hours.’

Three signs warn Plumridge about his workload: sleep, scheduling, and family. He knows he is doing too much when he gets less than six hours’ sleep for three consecutive nights, when he is constantly having to reschedule appointments, and when he misses a family birthday or anniversary. Then, he says, "I know things are out of control." Plumridge states that stress is often caused by his having unrealistic expectations of himself."I’ll promise a client that I’ll do something tomorrow, and then I’ll promise another client that I’ll do the same thing when I know it’s not going to happen. I could have said: ’Why don’t I give that to you in 48 hours?’ The client wouldn’t care."

Over-committing is something people experience as an individual problem. However, new research indicates that people may be designed to over-commit. A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology shows that people always believe that they will be less busy in the future. This is a misapprehension, according to the authors of the report, Gal Zauberman of the University of North Carolina and John Lynch of Duke University. On average, an individual will be just as busy two weeks or a month from now as he or she is today. But that is not how it appears in everyday life, they say."People make commitments long in advance that they would never make if the same commitments required immediate action. They discount future time investments relatively steeply."

Being too busy is highly subjective, but for any individual, there are some concrete signs of stress - disturbed sleep and declining mental and physical health are the most common examples. Figures for National Workers’ Compensation (insurance against injury caused by work) show that stress causes the most lost time of any workplace injury: employees suffering stress are absent from work for an average of 16.6 weeks. The effects of stress are also expensive. The Australian Government insurer reports that in 2003-2004, claims for stress-related psychological injury accounted for 7% of insurance claims but almost 27% of the amount paid out in claim payments.

Experts say the key to dealing with stress is not to focus on relief - a game of golf or a massage - but to reassess workloads. Neil Plumridge says he makes it a priority to work out what has to change: that might mean allocating extra staff to a job, allowing more time, or changing expectations. He also relies on the advice of colleagues, saying that his peers coach each other on business problems: "Just a fresh pair of eyes over an issue can help," he states.

Executive stress is not confined to big organisations. Vanessa Stoykov has been running her own advertising agency and public relations business for seven years. Her company has grown so fast that it appeared on the Business Review Weekly ’Fast 100’ list of fastest-growing small enterprises in 2004, just after Stoykov had her first child. In 2005, revenue was projected to double to $2.4 million. She had just had her second child. With a fast-growing business and two small children, Stoykov says she has mastered the art of caring for children, typing, and talking on the phone at the same time. But, unlike many others, she appears to thrive on the mental stimulation of running her own business, despite the stress.

Jan Elsner, a psychologist who specialises in executive coaching, says that doing well on a demanding workload is typical of senior executives. Some people work best with high-adrenaline periods followed by quieter times, while others thrive under sustained pressure. Elsner’s practice is based on a movement known as positive psychology, a school of thought that argues that positive experiences - feeling engaged and challenged, for example - do not balance out negative experiences such as stress; instead, they help people increase their resilience over time. Elsner says that many of the senior business people she coaches are increasingly relying more on regulating stress through methods such as meditation. She points to research showing that meditation can alter the biochemistry of the brain and the way that brains and bodies react to stress.

Some experts believe there is too much emphasis on treating job stress as an individual problem. Tony LaMontagne, of the University of Melbourne, says that while personality traits do have some effect on stress, it is systemic stressors - qualities of job roles and organisations themselves - that have a far greater effect. His recent research shows that the major predictor of stress is the level of job control a person has. The best type of job combines challenging work with high autonomy. The worst jobs combine challenging work and low control. People with demanding jobs but little autonomy have up to four times the probability of depression and more than double the risk of heart attack.

question_groups.instructions:
Look at the following statements and the list of people below.
Match each statement with the correct person.

questions.text: High-level workers tend to react positively to stress
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Người lao động cấp cao có xu hướng phản ứng tích cực với căng thẳng.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
senior executives ~ High-level workers
doing well, thrive ~ react positively
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Jan Elsner chỉ rõ: "làm tốt với khối lượng công việc đòi hỏi cao là điển hình của các giám đốc điều hành cấp cao... những người khác phát triển mạnh dưới áp lực duy trì." (doing well on a demanding workload is typical of senior executives... others thrive under sustained pressure.).
Bước 4: Đáp án: C
quotes: Jan Elsner, a psychologist who specialises in executive coaching, says that doing well on a demanding workload is typical of senior executives. Some people work best with high-adrenaline periods followed by quieter times, while others thrive under sustained pressure.

questions.text: Stress levels are increased by trying to please customers
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Mức độ căng thẳng tăng lên do cố gắng làm hài lòng khách hàng.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
promise a client, over-committing ~ trying to please customers
often caused by ~ increased by
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Neil Plumridge chỉ rõ: "Căng thẳng thường do ông có kỳ vọng không thực tế về bản thân. "Tôi sẽ hứa với một khách hàng rằng tôi sẽ làm điều gì đó vào ngày mai..." " (stress is often caused by his having unrealistic expectations of himself. "I'll promise a client that I'll do something tomorrow...")
Bước 4: Đáp án: A
quotes: Plumridge states that stress is often caused by his having unrealistic expectations of himself. "I’ll promise a client that I’ll do something tomorrow, and then I’ll promise another client that I’ll do the same thing when I know it’s not going to happen.

questions.text: Support from other workers may relieve stress
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Sự hỗ trợ từ các đồng nghiệp có thể giảm bớt căng thẳng.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
relies on the advice of colleagues, peers coach each other ~ Support from other workers
can help ~ relieve stress
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Neil Plumridge chỉ rõ: "Ông cũng dựa vào lời khuyên của đồng nghiệp, nói rằng đồng nghiệp huấn luyện lẫn nhau về các vấn đề kinh doanh: "chỉ cần một cặp mắt mới nhìn vào vấn đề có thể giúp ích," ông nói." (He also relies on the advice of colleagues, saying that his peers coach each other on business problems: "Just a fresh pair of eyes over an issue can help," he states.)
Bước 4: Đáp án: A
quotes: He also relies on the advice of colleagues, saying that his peers coach each other on business problems: "Just a fresh pair of eyes over an issue can help," he states.

questions.text: Lack of independence at work is often responsible for stress
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Thiếu sự độc lập trong công việc thường là nguyên nhân gây ra căng thẳng.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
low control, little autonomy ~ Lack of independence
major predictor of stress ~ responsible for stress
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Tony LaMontagne chỉ rõ: "Nghiên cứu gần đây của ông cho thấy yếu tố dự báo chính của căng thẳng là mức độ kiểm soát công việc mà một người có... Những công việc tồi tệ nhất kết hợp công việc đầy thử thách và kiểm soát thấp." (His recent research shows that the major predictor of stress is the level of job control a person has... The worst jobs combine challenging work and low control.)
Bước 4: Đáp án: D
quotes: His recent research shows that the major predictor of stress is the level of job control a person has. The best type of job combines challenging work with high autonomy. The worst jobs combine challenging work and low control. People with demanding jobs but little autonomy have up to four times the probability of depression and more than double the risk of heart attack.

questions.text: Workers commonly expect their workloads to lessen over time
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Người lao động thường mong đợi khối lượng công việc của họ sẽ giảm bớt theo thời gian.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
people always believe ~ Workers commonly expect
will be less busy in the future ~ workloads to lessen over time
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Gal Zauberman và John Lynch chỉ rõ: "Một nghiên cứu... cho thấy mọi người luôn tin rằng họ sẽ bớt bận rộn hơn trong tương lai." (A study... shows that people always believe that they will be less busy in the future.)
Bước 4: Đáp án: B
quotes: A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology shows that people always believe that they will be less busy in the future.

question_groups.instructions:
For questions 6-8, choose the correct letter A, B, C, or D.
Write the correct letter A-D on your answer sheet.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT mentioned by Neil Plumridge as an indication that his workload is too heavy?

options.label: A
options.text: an inability to keep to his schedule

options.label: C
options.text: a lack of concentration on a task

quotes: Three signs warn Plumridge about his workload: sleep, scheduling, and family. He knows he is doing too much when he gets less than six hours’ sleep for three consecutive nights, when he is constantly having to reschedule appointments, and when he misses a family birthday or anniversary.

questions.text: Which method of lessening work stress is NOT suggested by Neil Plumridge?

options.label: A
options.text: rethinking ideas of what can be achieved

options.label: B
options.text: extending the deadline for completing the task

options.label: C
options.text: using more workers on a project

options.label: D
options.text: taking more time off for sport or other recreation

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu và tìm keywords trong câu hỏi:
Phương pháp giảm căng thẳng công việc nào KHÔNG được Neil Plumridge đề xuất?
Bước 2: Tìm thông tin dựa trên keywords:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ Neil Plumridge nói:
"...phân bổ thêm nhân viên cho một công việc" (...allocating extra staff to a job) -> Đáp án C
"...cho phép thêm thời gian" (...allowing more time) -> Đáp án B
"...hoặc thay đổi kỳ vọng." (...or changing expectations.) -> Đáp án A
==> Neil Plumridge không đề cập đến việc nghỉ ngơi nhiều hơn cho thể thao hoặc giải trí khác.
Bước 3: Đáp án: D
Bước 4: Giải thích đáp án gây nhiễu:
Đáp án A: Xem xét lại ý tưởng về những gì có thể đạt được (rethinking ideas of what can be achieved) -> changing expectations.
Đáp án B: Kéo dài thời hạn hoàn thành nhiệm vụ (extending the deadline for completing the task) -> allowing more time.
Đáp án C: Sử dụng thêm người lao động trong một dự án (using more workers on a project) -> allocating extra staff.
quotes: Experts say the key to dealing with stress is not to focus on relief - a game of golf or a massage - but to reassess workloads. Neil Plumridge says he makes it a priority to work out what has to change: that might mean allocating extra staff to a job, allowing more time, or changing expectations.

questions.text: According to Jan Elsner, meditation offers a method of

options.label: A
options.text: taking a worker's mind off his troubles

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu và tìm keywords trong câu hỏi:
Theo Jan Elsner, thiền cung cấp một phương pháp để:
Bước 2: Tìm thông tin dựa trên keywords:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: "Bà ấy chỉ ra nghiên cứu cho thấy thiền có thể thay đổi hóa sinh của não và cách não và cơ thể phản ứng với căng thẳng." (She points to research showing that meditation can alter the biochemistry of the brain and the way that brains and bodies react to stress.).
==> Thông tin được in đậm đồng nghĩa với câu B (thay đổi phản ứng vật lý/thể chất đối với căng thẳng).
Bước 3: Đáp án: B
Bước 4: Giải thích đáp án gây nhiễu:
Đáp án A, C, D: Mặc dù thiền có thể bao hàm các hành động này, nhưng bà Elsner nhấn mạnh vào bằng chứng khoa học về việc thay đổi phản ứng sinh học và thể chất, khiến B là đáp án chính xác nhất.
quotes: She points to research showing that meditation can alter the biochemistry of the brain and the way that brains and bodies react to stress.
